answer: In an agent economy, one-account-one-vote is a relic: each agent must lock tokens for 90 days, and its voting power equals its locked stake. An attacker can forge a thousand identities, but splitting the same tokens among them adds no influence, leaving the swarm hollow. To control a majority, the attacker must acquire and lock more tokens than all honest voters combined, tying up capital and bearing the risk of a price collapse.
